title: TTL, garbage collection and the break-glass log
summary: Implement retention, reclamation, immediate wipe, quotas, and privacy-safe operational access records.

specReferences.heading: W12 · TTL, garbage collection and the break-glass log

produces: Reachability garbage collection and upload grace period

conditions: Reachability collection honors the upload grace window.
DELETE has no grace period and removes the store immediately.
Raw device IDs never appear in logs.
Retention statements match observed service behavior.
completion.summary: Athenaeum now enforces rolling retention, grace-aware reachability collection, immediate whole-store deletion, aggregate quotas, and privacy-safe operational logging.
evidence: server/test/athenaeum_store_test.dart proves reachable and recent uploads survive collection, stale uploads are reclaimed after the grace window, and repeated uploads do not renew uploaded_at.
server/test/athenaeum_app_test.dart proves DELETE /v1/store removes a grace-protected blob immediately and aggregate quota failures return 507 before persistent allocation.

server/test/athenaeum_app_test.dart and server/test/athenaeum_store_test.dart prove diagnostic records omit raw manifest device IDs and credentials, persist only derived identifiers, remain bounded and indexed, and expire during the hourly sweep.
docs/dev/store-submission/privacy-policy.md, site/privacy/index.html, and server/README.md state the observed 30-day eligibility and next-hourly-sweep pruning behavior consistently.
